metadata.title: MU, SNDK, SKHY Stocks Bounce After Thursday’s Markdown, But Strategists Split: ‘Great Buying Opportunity’ Versus ‘The Kospi Has Peaked’

content.text:
-

-
Mowrey pointed to weakening commodity prices and the possibility of disinflation in 2027.
Memory stocks Micron Technology (MU), SanDisk (SNDK) and SK Hynix (SKHY) rebounded in early trading Friday after a sharp sell-off a day earlier, but strategists remain divided over whether the pullback presents a buying opportunity or signals a broader market peak.
MU stock was up over 1%, SNDK stock gained nearly 2%, while SKHY shares jumped over 4%. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around Micron remained in 'bearish' territory over the past day, while sentiment around SanDisk and SK Hynix trended in the 'bullish' zone.
The rebound comes after the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (SOX) fell 6.7% in the previous session, its worst day since June 23, and Micron lost about 6%.
In an interview with CNBC, Chris Verrone, chief market strategist at Strategas, said the damage looks technical, not fundamental, and argued that further weakness would be short-lived. Meanwhile, John Mowrey, chief investment officer at NFJ Investment Group, took the opposite view on memory and on the Korean market that depends on it.
Strategist Sees Semiconductor Sell-Off Creating Buying Opportunity
According to Verrone, the recent weakness in semiconductor stocks does not reflect a comparable deterioration in the underlying business outlook.
"Fundamentally, we're seeing great strength, but technically, there's some pressure on these semiconductors, and if the pressure continues, it could take the market on a little leg lower, which I think will be quick and a great buying opportunity," he said.
The pullback follows a period when technology stocks led the broader market higher. Verrone said the speed of the reversal had caught investors' attention. The SOX is now more than 26% below its June 22 record.
Verrone also pointed to a shift in market leadership. Defensive sectors have strengthened even as technology stocks have weakened, with consumer staples and health care hitting records Thursday while the Nasdaq Composite fell 2.6%. "Right now, defenses are leading. That's got my spidey sense up," he said. "Like this is not the leadership we want to see, and we have to watch semiconductors."
